facts.text: Auburn was incorporated as a city on February 22, 1869, becoming the first in Maine to adopt a council‑manager government.
In 1835, the first shoe‑manufacturing factory system began in Auburn, and by 1917 a single plant produced 75% of the world’s white canvas shoes.
The Androscoggin River powered Auburn’s early mills, and the 1823 bridge to Lewiston helped the town grow into a mill hub.
Two bronze water sculptures—Falls Fountain and Shoe Fountain—decorate Auburn’s downtown, honoring the river and its shoe‑making heritage.
Auburn’s name comes from the village Auburn mentioned in Oliver Goldsmith’s 1770 poem “The Deserted Village.”.
The town’s historic Knight House Museum, built in 1796, is the oldest frame house downtown and once housed a hand‑work shoe shop.
